sentences.text: MFA No.21390/2013 is filed by the claimant for seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. Factum of accident and the deceased died in the accident are not disputed.
The disputed fact is that, the offending vehicle Tempo Trax is used on hire and contract basis and thus, it is contended that Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
4. The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.1,65,000/- and held appellant-Insurance Company liable to pay the compensation.

5. From the complaint-Ex.P2, FIR-Ex.P1 and charge sheet-Ex.P7, it is proved that the deceased and others have taken the tempo trax on hire basis for traveling to Shrishail to participate in a jatra celebration and while NC: 2023:KHC-D:10602 returning from Shrishail, the tempo trax met with accident and the deceased died.
Therefore, it is proved that tempo trax was used on hire and contract basis, it violated the conditions of Insurance policy.
Therefore, the appellant insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner.
6. The deceased was 58 years old women being an agriculturist and home maker.
The accident is occurred in the year 2011.
Therefore, notional income would be taken at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Just because, the deceased being woman and home maker cannot be said that she was not contributing the income to the family.
Therefore, the compensation awarded under the head loss of dependency is lesser side.
There are three legal heirs who are husband and children.
Therefore, 1/3 amount is deducted towards personal expenses.
Appropriate multiplier is 9.

Therefore, loss of dependency is reassessed and quantified as below:
Rs.6,000/-+600X2/3X9X12 = 4,75,200/-.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10602 7.
Further, for transportation of dead body and funeral expenses Rs.15,000 + 10% escalation, in total Rs.16,500/- is awarded.
8. Further, for loss of estate Rs.15,000 + 10% escalation, total of Rs.16,500/- is awarded.
9. Further, Rs.1,32,000/- (Rs.40,000X3+10% escalation) is awarded under the head loss of consortium.

10. Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:

In the present case, tempo trax is used for hire and contract basis.
Therefore, is used for the purpose other NC: 2023:KHC-D:10602 than permit.

Therefore, insurance company is rightly observed that as per Sub-section (2) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, when the Insurance Company established the fact that driver was not holding driving license, then as per Sub-sections (1), (5), (7) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, the Insurance Company as if the judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim in respect of third parties and then recover the same from owner of the offending vehicle.

12. Accordingly, order of pay and recovery is made as per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Pappu and others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another1 and also as per the full bench decision of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Bijapur vs. Yallavva w/o.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Both appeals are allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 09.10.2012 passed in MVC.No.139/2011 by the District Judge and MACT, Gadag is modified to the above extent.
iii) The insurance company shall pay compensation within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment as awarded by this court to claimants at the first instance and then recover the same from owner of offending vehicle bearing No.KA-29/MA 6500.
iv) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,40,200-00 along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization as against NC: 2023:KHC-D:10602 compensation of Rs.1,65,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

viii) No order as to costs.
 ix) Draw award accordingly.
